edges.description: Supplying wild-type NDUFAF3 to the patient's own cells is what localises the enzyme deficiency to this gene rather than to a coincidental variant, and it was the basis on which the founding alleles were called pathogenic.
edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are not neurons, and the affected tissues - basal ganglia, brainstem, white matter - have never been studied in this disease. The rescue establishes causality; it says nothing about why those structures fail, nor about the threshold of residual complex I activity a neuron tolerates. The 2023 patient's fibroblasts show only a mild activity reduction alongside a severe complexome defect, which is a direct demonstration that the fibroblast activity assay can under-read this disease.

edges.description: Depleting NDUFAF3 abolishes complex I assembly and shortens the half-life of newly synthesised ND1 fourfold, and knocking down the protease restores it.
edges.limitations: Knockdown is not a patient genotype. Every reported human allele is missense, in-frame, splice-site or initiation-codon rather than a null, and the missense alleles may leave partial function, so the magnitude of the ND1 effect in knockdown cells is an upper bound on what happens in a patient. The cells are also not an affected tissue.

edges.description: Losing either factor impairs biogenesis of the Q-, N- and PP-b-modules. Forced expression of NDUFAF4 rescues the Q-module defect caused by loss of NDUFAF3, which is direct in vivo evidence that the two act in one pathway, and raises the possibility that some NDUFAF3 missense alleles could be rescued by raising NDUFAF4.
edges.limitations: Drosophila, and no human variant is modelled - the manipulation is RNAi knockdown of the fly orthologue, not knock-in of a patient allele. The module nomenclature also does not map cleanly onto the human patient data: the fly work reports impaired Q-, N- and PP-b module biogenesis, while the patient gels show Q- and P-module subunits depleted together with early membrane-arm sub-assemblies accumulating. Both place the lesion early; neither settles the order of events.

nodes.description: Two damaged copies of NDUFAF3 (C3ORF60), which encodes a mitochondrial complex I assembly factor. The reported alleles span several mutation classes. The ClinGen expert-panel curation scored six variants across the first three reports: four missense changes, one initiation-codon change and one in-frame duplication. The leukoencephalopathy patient carries the in-frame duplication c.342_343insGTG p.117Valdup in trans with the missense c.505C>A p.Pro169Thr; the 2023 patient carries a splice-site variant in trans with a missense variant. No clean null allele has been reported.

nodes.description: NDUFAF3's place in complex I biogenesis is on the earliest assembly intermediates. It co-immunoprecipitates with NDUFAF4 and with the matrix-arm subunits NDUFS2, NDUFA9 and NDUFS3 in a roughly 400 kDa intermediate that also contains the mitochondrially encoded ND1 subunit. Losing it therefore removes a component from the step at which the nuclear-encoded matrix arm and the mtDNA-encoded membrane arm are first brought together.

This is the experiment that made NDUFAF3 a disease gene: baculovirus-delivered NDUFAF3-GFP in the founding report, and an independent complementation in the Leigh-syndrome patient's fibroblasts nine years later. There is no NDUFAF3 mouse, and no patient tissue beyond the muscle and fibroblast samples of the published cases.

The severe pole, and what most reported children have had. The gene was found in three families with severe neonatal lactic acidosis, and across the first seven reported patients the course was severe neurological disease with lactic acidosis, fatal in infancy in most. The expert-panel summary adds the features seen as that course runs: developmental regression, hypotonia and myoclonic seizures, with onset between the neonatal period and early childhood.

nodes.description: The holoenzyme does not complete. Two-dimensional blue-native and denaturing gels from the leukoencephalopathy patient show matrix-arm Q-module subunits (NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFA9) and membrane-arm P-module subunits (NDUFB10, NDUFB11) reduced together, so the block is not confined to one module. Complexome profiling of the 2023 patient shows what piles up behind it: early membrane-arm sub-assemblies still bound to the MCIA complex. The same profiling reports a second, unusual species in that patient - free monomeric complex I still holding the MCIA complex and other assembly factors - so the holoenzyme that does form has not released its assembly machinery.
